title: Degree-zero constant direct images under connected fibres
statement: Let f : X → S be a flat quasi-compact morphism of schemes with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. For any commutative ring R in the coefficient universe and any R-module M whose underlying set is finite, the degree-zero higher direct image of the constant M sheaf is constructible. The direct image and constructibility use [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]; geometric stalks use [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. This statement uses the source-library constructibility predicate for modules over any ring, not an assumption that R is finite.

proof.text:
apply the connected-fibre section theorem to the pullback over every etale
object of the base. Its section map is the component of the inverse-image adjunction
unit, followed by restriction along the identity chart. That restriction is an
isomorphism, so the unit is an isomorphism objectwise and hence as a sheaf morphism.
The degree-zero derived functor is the underived direct image. Inverse image preserves
constant sheaves, so its value on the constant sheaf is the base constant sheaf.
This is finite locally constant: identity charts prove local constancy, and the
constant-stalk comparison gives finite stalks. The trivial stratification proves
constructibility. The proof includes empty bases and zero coefficient modules.

theorem higherDirectImage_zero_constant_constructible
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing R]
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [QuasiCompact f] [GeometricallyConnected f]
    (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) [Finite M] :
    Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf (higherDirectImage R f 0
      ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R)).obj M))
